specimens.title: The specimen: add()
specimens.blurb: One line of C++. At -O0 every variable lives in memory and a*2 is a mul. At -O2 it is three instructions and a shift.
specimens.ir_O0:
define i32 @add(i32 %0, i32 %1) {
  %3 = alloca i32, align 4
  %4 = alloca i32, align 4
  store i32 %0, ptr %3, align 4
  store i32 %1, ptr %4, align 4
  %5 = load i32, ptr %3, align 4
  %6 = mul nsw i32 %5, 2
  %7 = load i32, ptr %4, align 4
  %8 = add nsw i32 %6, %7
  ret i32 %8
}

specimens.title: A template that disappears
specimens.blurb: Complex<T> with operator overloads, the fractal's inner loop. At -O0 you see calls to operator* and operator+. At -O2 they are gone: one loop of f64.mul and f64.add. "Zero-cost abstraction" is inlining plus SROA.

specimens.title: Computed at build time
specimens.blurb: The same colour, two ways. red_runtime() does the arithmetic every call. red() reads a table the compiler filled in: 768 bytes in the .wasm data section, no math left. Constant folding, taken to its limit.

specimens.title: A virtual call becomes call_indirect
specimens.blurb: Shape::area() through a base pointer. The vtable is data, the targets live in a function table, and the call is call_indirect with a type: the engine checks the signature at every call. That check is part of what makes it safe.
